PullRequest.Title: chat: replace sandboxed label with icon
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace the visible `(sandboxed)` permission label with a shield icon for the Copilot harness
- use the key icon for Manual permissions in Chat and the Agents Window
- preserve the sandboxed state in accessible labels and tooltips
- keep Claude and Codex permission presentation unchanged

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- 53 focused Agent Host and permission picker tests
- targeted stylelint for the changed stylesheets
- Agents Window permission picker fixtures render without errors

Fixes #333929

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75a501f4-9404-40b0-936d-96bf04ec73a8

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update the sandboxed permission trigger in the Sessions/Agents Window picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A picker render, permission-level observable update, managed-sandbox update, or relevant configuration event synchronously clears and rebuilds the single trigger before the UI reflects the state. Hover text is resolved only after mouse-over and is off the initial render critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One permission picker per active session surface; sandboxing adds exactly one icon DOM node. Cost scales with low-frequency permission/configuration changes, not messages, history items, repositories, or tool calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM mutation and hover resolution run serially on the UI event loop. Observable/configuration updates can cause another rebuild, but each picker owns one trigger and its DisposableStore removes prior listeners and nodes before replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Permission metadata and localized strings are computed locally; configuration reads use the in-memory consolidated configuration model. There is no network/filesystem cache or miss path introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed render method, observable/configuration listeners, hover callback, and disposal path were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/reflow time varies by host and theme, but the changed DOM cardinality is fixed at one node and no realistic multiplicity was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Before the PR the trigger rebuilt an icon and text label; after it conditionally rebuilds one additional shield icon while shortening the visible text. The new hover check performs bounded in-memory reads only and introduces no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and hover the Agent Host AutoApprove chip in a workbench chat input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session attachment/config resolution is the existing prerequisite for a chip to have context. Once context exists, the changed path synchronously renders the trigger and one conditional shield icon; tooltip content is now computed on mouse-over, off the initial-render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the initial agent session configuration through the agent-host protocol client for an untitled session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight resolve per picker/session attachment; prior requests are cancelled on session changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolveSessionConfig call occurred before this PR with identical placement and cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite for first meaningful chip render on an untitled session; the shield/icon and hover changes neither add nor repeat it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or obtain the provisional backend session used by untitled chat-input pickers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Racing picker instances are serialized/coalesced by the provisional service to one provisional session per untitled session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same getOrCreate call and service-level coalescing existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous initialization; rendering proceeds without awaiting it and rerenders when the service signals completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The changed shield allocation applies only to the single AutoApprove chip when sandboxing is enabled. Rebuild count follows session/config state changes; it does not scale with dynamic enum size or chat history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM render and delayed-hover callbacks are serialized on the UI thread. Existing initial config resolves are cancellation-bounded per picker, and provisional creation is serialized/coalesced by the service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Active-session context is read from an existing subscription or provisional resolved-config state. Sandbox settings are read synchronously from in-memory configuration. Cold untitled sessions use the existing resolve/provisional paths; warm subscribed sessions reuse current state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor/reattach, render/disposal, hover-service invocation, in-memory configuration implementation, and IPC service delegation were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host resolve duration depends on provider and environment, but that boundary is unchanged. The changed rendering and hover work remains constant-sized.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR adds one disposable DOM icon and moves tooltip formatting from eager render-time computation to delayed hover-time computation; it does not increase existing IPC cardinality or place it on a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display the same permission controls in compact responsive layouts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS selector matching and layout occur during the existing trigger render; compact mode hides the newly added sandbox icon with display:none.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One hidden shield node per sandboxed permission trigger, with a small fixed number of permission controls in a toolbar.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style and layout work is serialized with the existing UI render; no timers, queues, or parallel external work are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static stylesheet and codicon font resources use the existing application resource pipeline; the diff adds no resource fetch or cache key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both CSS hunks and their corresponding trigger construction paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser selector/layout costs vary, but the selectors are shallow class selectors and node count is constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra hidden element is constant-sized and lifecycle-bounded, with no collection-scale selector or repeated forced layout mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files and all diff pages. The changes add constant-sized icon presentation and delayed tooltip formatting, with proper disposal and no newly introduced subprocess, filesystem, database, network, or IPC work. Existing agent-host initialization boundaries retain their pre-diff cardinality and scheduling.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
